description: Different resolution in subtitle vs video — both should strip resolution and match by base name
notes: Video base = 'Movie' (720p stripped). Subtitle base = 'Movie' (1080p stripped). Bases match despite different resolutions.

description: CJK name video and subtitle — exact CJK match required
notes: Video base = '蜘蛛侠.2002'. Subtitle base = '蜘蛛侠.2002'. Bases match. Only zh-Hans available, no en or vi.

description: Year preserved in base name — resolution stripped, year kept
notes: Video base = 'Movie.2023' (1080p stripped). Subtitle base = 'Movie.2023'. Year is part of base name, not stripped.

description: Video with no resolution suffix — base name is entire filename minus extension
notes: No resolution to strip. Video base = 'Movie'. Direct match with subtitle base 'Movie'.

description: Spaces in both video and subtitle filenames
notes: Space separator. Video base = 'My Movie' (1080p stripped with space delimiter). Subtitle base = 'My Movie'.

description: Dots as separators in both video and subtitle
notes: Dot separator. Video base = 'My.Movie' (1080p stripped). Subtitle base = 'My.Movie'.

description: Multiple .en.srt files with version suffix — sort alphabetically, pick first
notes: Both match 'en'. Alphabetical sort: 'Movie.en.srt' < 'Movie.en-2.srt'. First is target, second is in others.

description: Subtitle in subfolder — algorithm must search subfolders like 'subs/'
notes: Subtitle in 'subs/' subfolder. Common in scene releases (Movie.2023.1080p.BluRay.x264/Subs/). Algorithm must traverse subfolders.

description: No subtitle at all — graceful null return
notes: Empty subtitle list. Algorithm must handle gracefully — return all nulls.

description: Completely different base name — no match
notes: Video base = 'Movie'. Subtitle base = 'OtherMovie'. No match — subtitle is for a different video.

description: 4K suffix NOT stripped — base name retains _4K
notes: 4K is not NNNp pattern, so NOT stripped. Video base = 'Movie_4K'. Subtitle base = 'Movie_4K'. Match succeeds because neither is stripped.

description: Bilingual SRT — single file with target+native interleaved, no language code
notes: Single bilingual SRT with no language code. Fallback subtitle serves as both target and native. Algorithm should return same file for both.

description: Case mismatch between video and subtitle base names
notes: Video base = 'Movie'. Subtitle base = 'movie'. Case-insensitive comparison required for base name matching.

description: Uppercase P in resolution — case-insensitive resolution strip
notes: Video has '1080P' (uppercase P). Resolution strip must be case-insensitive. Video base = 'Movie'. Subtitle base = 'Movie'.

description: HDR suffix NOT stripped — base name retains .HDR
notes: HDR is not a resolution pattern, NOT stripped. Video base = 'Movie.HDR'. Subtitle base = 'Movie.HDR'. Match succeeds.

description: Director's Cut with spaces — resolution stripped, edition text preserved
notes: Video base = 'Movie Directors Cut 2009' (1080p stripped). Subtitle base = 'Movie Directors Cut'. MISMATCH — subtitle lacks year. No match unless algorithm does fuzzy/partial matching.

description: Anime bracket naming — group and resolution in brackets stripped
notes: Video base = '[Group] Movie - 01' (bracketed [1080p] stripped). Subtitle base = 'Movie - 01'. MISMATCH — subtitle lacks [Group] prefix. No match unless algorithm strips bracketed group tags.

description: Complex WEB-DL naming with NF source — resolution is split point
notes: Video base = 'Movie.2023' (1080p and trailing NF.WEB-DL stripped). Subtitle base = 'Movie.2023'. Match. Only vi available, no en.

description: Long dot-separated title — resolution is split point, year preserved
notes: Video base = 'Movie.Title.with.many.dots.2023' (1080p.WEB-DL stripped). Subtitle base = 'Movie.Title.with.many.dots.2023'. Exact match.

description: CJK title with BCP 47 script subtag subtitle
notes: Video base = '蜘蛛侠.2002' (1080p stripped). Subtitle base = '蜘蛛侠'. MISMATCH — subtitle lacks year '2002'. No match unless algorithm does partial CJK matching. Only zh-Hans available, no en or vi.
